patients.summary: 34-year-old retail store manager with iron deficiency anemia on oral iron and obesity, two prior cesareans before joining in 2021. Three pregnancies under the practice each ended in uterine rupture at term at an outside hospital (2023, 2024, 2026); the third required cesarean hysterectomy and transfusion. Now recovering with improving hemoglobin.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is Gladys Perez, 29, wants to join the practice. Moved her care after her last doctor's office stopped taking her Medicaid plan. Had a baby in March by C-section, says she is doing fine, takes iron and vitamins. Asked if we can see her in the evening because she works at the store until 6 most days. Offered Tues 9/14 at 4:30, she took it. Sent new patient packet and records release to her email. Reminded her to bring all pill bottles.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establish care

29F here to set up primary care. Last PCP was a family practice in town; leaving because of insurance. She is 6 months out from her second C-section (March 2021). Feels well. Main ongoing issue is anemia — told she was low on iron with her first pregnancy in 2019 and has been on iron ever since. Takes ferrous sulfate three times a day, a prenatal vitamin with iron, and calcium twice a day, all of which her OB started and she has kept going. No other complaints today.

PMH: iron deficiency anemia; obesity.
PSH: low transverse cesarean x2 — 2019 and March 2021. No other surgery.
OB: two deliveries, both by cesarean, both term per pt.
Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tab daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID; calcium carbonate 600 mg BID.
Allergies: SULFA drugs (reaction not recorded).
FHx: mother needed a C-section for placenta previa. Maternal aunt had a uterine rupture during labor. No other family history she knows of.
SHx: manages a retail store, long shifts on her feet. Married, lives in Springfield. Never smoked. No alcohol. No drugs.
Immunizations: COVID Pfizer x2 this spring (April and May, at the pharmacy). Flu shot usually yearly.

ROS: no chest pain, no dyspnea, no palpitations, no abdominal pain. Neg otherwise per intake form.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Ht 159.5 cm, wt 87.5 kg, BMI 34.4.
Gen: pleasant, no distress.
HEENT: conjunctivae slightly pale, oropharynx clear.
Neck: supple, thyroid not enlarged.
CV: regular, no murmur.
Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, nontender, healed low transverse incision.
Ext: warm, no edema.
Skin: no rash.
Psych: normal mood and affect.

PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. Iron deficiency anemia on oral iron — CBC and iron studies today. Continue ferrous sulfate 325 TID for now.
2. Obesity, BMI 34 — discussed in general terms, she is busy with two small kids and work; will revisit.
3. Hx cesarean x2 — noted.
4. Health maintenance — CMP, TSH, A1c, lipids. Offered one-time HIV and hep C screen, she agreed. Pap: says last one was 2019 and normal, will confirm with records. Flu shot next month when stock arrives.
5. Records request to prior practice signed today.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Results from new patient labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Gladys, your labs from Tuesday are in. Your blood count is still a little low (hemoglobin 11.3) and your iron stores are low (ferritin 10), which fits with having had a baby in March. Keep taking the iron three times a day with the vitamin. Kidney, liver, sugar, thyroid and cholesterol all look fine, and the HIV and hepatitis C tests are negative. We'll recheck the blood count in about 6 months.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
38 pages received by fax from prior family practice, scanned to media. Summary for PCP:
- Problem list: iron deficiency anemia (noted during 2019 pregnancy), obesity.
- Surgical: cesarean delivery 04/2019; repeat low transverse cesarean 03/2021 (operative notes not included, discharge summary from 2021 included — uncomplicated repeat cesarean).
- Meds on file: prenatal vitamin with iron, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, calcium carbonate 600 mg BID.
- Allergy: sulfa.
- Pap smear 08/2019: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Last CBC 05/2021: hemoglobin low, on oral iron.
Nothing else of note. Records request closed.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after work for flu vaccine. Not breastfeeding per pt. No fever today, no prior vaccine reactions. Sulfa allergy noted, not relevant. Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM R deltoid, VIS provided. Tolerated without issue, waited 15 min, left ambulatory.

documents.title: Ferrous sulfate refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pharmacy fax: ferrous sulfate 325 mg tab, 1 TID, #90 x 5 refills requested — prior Rx was from outside prescriber. Pended for PCP.

PCP: approved, sent.

documents.title: No-show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 4:30 appt. Called cell, left VM to reschedule. Text sent as well.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back for anemia check, missed the slot two weeks ago because of inventory at work. Taking ferrous sulfate three times a day plus the prenatal and calcium. Energy okay. No bleeding issues she has noticed.

O: Vitals reviewed. Wt 87.4 kg.
No pallor today. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abd soft.

A/P: Iron deficiency anemia — repeat CBC and iron panel today, expect slow improvement. Continue current iron. Obesity — weight about the same, we talked about walking on her days off. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Blood count and iron
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gladys — hemoglobin is up to 12.4 from 11.3, which is in the normal range, and ferritin is 18, up from 10. Iron stores are still on the low side, so moving in the right direction but not done. Same iron dose, recheck at your physical.

documents.title: RE: Blood count and iron
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thank you!! will keep taking them

documents.title: Prenatal vitamin coverage
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy reports Medicaid plan now needs a prescription on file for the prenatal vitamin with iron to cover it (previously filled from old OB Rx, expired). Pended new Rx, 1 tab daily, #30 x 11 for PCP. PCP signed. Pharmacy notified, claim went through.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

30 y/o here for physical. Doing well. Still on ferrous sulfate TID, prenatal with iron, calcium BID. No new symptoms. Kids are 3 and 1 now, work is busy with the holiday season starting.

Meds and allergies reviewed (sulfa). Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: Wt 89.1 kg. Well appearing.
HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement.
Heart: RRR, no murmur. Lungs: clear bilat.
Breasts: deferred per pt preference, no concerns.
Abd: soft, nontender, well-healed Pfannenstiel scar.
Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal appearing, Pap/HPV collected.
Ext: no edema.

PHQ-2: 1.

A/P
- Preventive: Pap with HPV co-test today (last 2019 normal). CBC, iron, CMP, lipids, A1c.
- Iron deficiency anemia: recheck today on TID iron.
- Obesity: wt 89.1, up slightly. Encouraged activity, fewer sugary drinks at work.
- Flu and bivalent COVID booster given today.
RTC 1 year or sooner.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news on the physical labs. Hemoglobin 12.4, same as March, and ferritin 21, the best it has been since you joined us. Sugar, cholesterol, kidney and liver normal. Your Pap and HPV test are both negative, so the next one isn't due for 5 years. Keep going with the iron.
